title: A61 Anchor Map row
description: Schema for one row of analysis/canonical/core_controls/A61_anchor_map.csv. The anchor map is the canonical bridge between A59 evidence-bound claims and the diagram sidecars (c4-plantuml-from-context + camunda-bpmn-from-context, plus future DBML / sequence-diagram sidecars). Every diagram view-element traces back to an A61 row, which in turn traces back to a SourceClaimID in A59 — closing the diagram-to-evidence chain documented in skills/c4-plantuml-from-context/references/integration-contract.md ("canonical A59 claim → A61 anchor row → anchor_manifest.json entry → .puml view_element_id"). Producer: bsa-anchor-auditor (via the anchor-binding stage). Consumers: c4-plantuml-from-context + camunda-bpmn-from-context sidecars (orchestrated mode), plus the F5 hook layer's sibling-artifact cache when sidecar manifests need cross-referencing. Pre-v1.2.7 this schema did not exist and A61 was hand-rolled per fixture (closes the v1.2.6 sidecar-fixture forward-looking gap at fixtures/golden/project_0004_sidecar_e2e/README.md).

AnchorID.description: Stable identifier matching the per-sidecar anchor_manifest.schema.json a61_anchor_id pattern (^ANC-[A-Z0-9_-]+$). Conventional category prefixes (e.g., ANC-SYS-001 for systems, ANC-EVT-001 for BPMN events) are recommended but not enforced — the pattern is intentionally permissive so per-engagement vocabulary can extend without schema bumps.

AnchorKind.description: The kind of architecture / process element this anchor represents. Intentionally a loose identifier pattern (not an enum) so that BOTH C4-PlantUML conventions (camelCase or PascalCase: System, Person, Container, System_Boundary, Deployment_Node, Rel) AND BPMN conventions (camelCase: startEvent, task, sequenceFlow, exclusiveGateway, etc.) AND future sidecar conventions (DBML, sequence-diagram) can populate it without forcing a coupled-enum bump in this schema. The strict per-kind enum lives downstream in each sidecar's anchor_manifest.schema.json (view_element_kind for C4, element_kind for BPMN). A61 stays sidecar-agnostic by design — it is the shared bridge layer.

SourceClaimID.description: Foreign key into A59_claim_register.csv. Every anchor MUST trace back to an evidence-bound claim — anchors without a source claim would let diagrams over-reach beyond the canonical claim layer (the trace-chain invariant from skills/c4-plantuml-from-context/references/integration-contract.md §"Relationship to canonical claim-layer"). Same prefix conventions as A59.ClaimID (C-NNN or C-XXX-NNN). When a desired diagram element has no A59 backing claim, the anchor is NOT authored here — instead an A51 route is opened (IssueType=missing_source or boundary_risk) per the integration-contract escalation rule.

Label.description: Human-readable label (system name, actor role, BPMN task name, etc.) — what shows up in the diagram as the visible element name. Free-form but never empty; label-less anchors cannot be cross-referenced in diagram review.

Notes.description: Free-form analyst notes on the anchor's role / scope / boundaries. May be empty. Common content: which sidecar(s) consume this anchor, scoping caveats, cross-references to A51 routes for adjacent unresolved items.

x-bsa-csv-columns-order._comment: Canonical column order for A61 CSV. Producers should write columns in this order for stability; consumers tolerate any order via DictReader. The loader's iter_a61_rows enforces order on read for diff cleanliness (matches the x-bsa-csv-columns-order convention in a51/a58/a59/a60/a62/a70/a71/a72).

x-bsa-foreign-keys._comment: DOCUMENTARY backward-compat block. The v1.2.7 documentary FK block has been superseded by the EXECUTABLE `x-bsa-anchor-binding-rules` extension below (v1.2.8). Kept here so external tooling that read the v1.2.7 documentary block doesn't break — the FK semantic is unchanged, only the enforcement layer changed (documentary → executable). New tooling SHOULD read `x-bsa-anchor-binding-rules` instead.

SourceClaimID.rationale: Every anchor must trace back to an evidence-bound claim (no orphan anchors). Enforced executable in v1.2.8 via x-bsa-anchor-binding-rules below.

x-bsa-anchor-binding-rules._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer as of v1.2.8. Closes the two cross-row deferrals from v1.2.7: (a) every A61.SourceClaimID MUST resolve to an existing A59.ClaimID — orphan anchors would let diagrams over-reach beyond the canonical claim layer (the trace-chain invariant from skills/c4-plantuml-from-context/references/integration-contract.md §'Relationship to canonical claim-layer'); (b) every A61.AnchorID MUST be unique across rows — duplicate anchors would let two claims silently share one diagram element. Implementation: governance/schemas/write_validator.py::_apply_anchor_binding_rules + _SiblingArtifactCache (per-validation-run memoized sibling reads). Pre-v1.2.8 these were enforced only at the per-fixture test layer (test_fixture_a61_no_duplicate_anchor_ids) — v1.2.8 makes them mechanical at hook time so any writer (orchestrator, skill, operator manual edit) is gated. Same shape conventions as A72's x-bsa-foreign-key-rules (applies_to_all_rows gate; sibling-not-readable surfaces a clear violation).
x-bsa-anchor-binding-rules.rationale: Without these rules, A61 could emit phantom anchors (SourceClaimID points at a ClaimID A59 doesn't have) or shadow anchors (two rows share AnchorID, so two distinct claims silently project to the same diagram element). Both defeat A61's purpose as the canonical bridge between claims and diagrams.
